item.title: Coding gives you a window into what the future will look like for a large amount of knowledge work. The first step for most jobs is that we go from doing most of the research, typing, and value creation manually (even if it’s using digital tools) to soon coordinating the work that agents are doing...
item.description:
作者：Aaron Levie 账号：@levie 简介：ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
Coding gives you a window into what the future will look like for a large amount of knowledge work.
The first step for most jobs is that we go from doing most of the research, typing, and value creation manually (even if it’s using digital tools) to soon coordinating the work that agents are doing.
Next, as this step itself becomes redundant or slows down what agents are capable of, we will be giving agents goals to optimize against and they’ll go off on and increasingly solve larger problems for us.
This may at first blush look like something whose impact gets stuck with coding, but actually a large percentage of knowledge work may eventually just converge with this form factor due to the massive productivity gains that can be generated. Agents will use computers, leverage our existing tools or write new ones, and write code on the fly to solve larger swaths of knowledge work.
So even if a task today doesn’t seem to be “coding” directly, the task may eventually fold into being coding adjacent. Manufacturing, architecture, life sciences, material sciences, cyber, and on and on.
One big hurdle in the way ultimately will be that much of this work remains non-verifiable, so humans will be even more in the loop than they are in coding. But the part that they can hand off will just get bigger and bigger over time as the models are more capable.
So in short, pay attention to coding and you’ll get a sense for where work is going.

item.title: I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :) - 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC... - Real eleva...
item.description:
作者：Andrej Karpathy 账号：@karpathy
I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :)
- 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC... - Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid. - The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc. - 19 lenses (income, degrees, faith, disasters…), a City View for 524 metros, and nine advisors plus an Explorer. The Explorer turns any column for any of 3,100+ counties into a table and scatter plot, linked to the map. - Claude decided to skip a few states and territories sry - Built using Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on medium and turning on ultracode.
It's deployed here: https://t.co/QMhmafXMj5 and the "?" has the source link too. I don't exactly know where I was going with this but it's really fun to browse and play with. Possibly it can be expanded or built into a game. I only have half of my weekly Claude quote left though so someone else will have to take over :D. Claude also made a trailer:

item.title: AI native teams will eventually force the surrounding organization to become AI native too. Take software development. coding velocity is way up thanks to AI, while actual shipped products and business impact are unchanged in most companies. That’s cos the surrounding system of experimentation tool...
item.description:
作者：Madhu Guru 账号：@realmadhuguru 简介：Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
AI native teams will eventually force the surrounding organization to become AI native too.
Take software development. coding velocity is way up thanks to AI, while actual shipped products and business impact are unchanged in most companies. That’s cos the surrounding system of experimentation tooling, evaluation, launch processes, and gtm are outdated.
It’s like sticking a Ferrari engine in a sedan and racing it on Indian roads. The engine can rev faster but the car speed is limited by its system and environment.
AI native companies were built ground up for this new way of building and shipping. They’re also able to shed suboptimal processes faster.
Market forces will quickly force all companies to adapt or perish.
If you’re solving this for your company: map out your product lifecycle and rebuild it ground up - tooling, team structure, gtm, everything.

item.title: OpenAI’s Noam Brown: Why Game Theory Didn’t Lead to General Intelligence (Live at No Limit Finals)
item.description:
播客：Training Data
Speaker 1 | 00:00 - 00:22 Please join me in a round of applause for Noam and Alfred. Hey, Noam. Thank you for coming. It's been a rainy day, and this is this is actually all because of you, because you started studying poker for a while. You and I talked a little bit about your research before you went to OpenAI.
Speaker 1 | 00:22 - 00:35 You went from studying poker to studying game theory and diplomacy to now reasoning. Like, what... Tell us about... A little bit about your path. Why did you decide to study poker of all all things?
